guitar.notes: Confirmed — Billy Gibbons' 1959 Les Paul "Pearly Gates" is one of the most famous guitars in rock history.

tone.target: snappy crunchy ZZ Top riff tone with slight fuzz and tight mids
tone.profile: snappy crunchy ZZ Top riff tone with slight fuzz and tight mids
tone.summary: A punchy rhythm tone built with Fuzz for texture, Comp for attack definition, followed by a UK 45 or UK 50 model to achieve the desired Plexi/Marshall grit and tight mids. Minimal effects are used to maintain dryness.

rig.name: ZZ Top - Sharp Dressed Man - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and maintain tight riff definition.
Enhance the attack and punch of the rhythm guitar riffs.
Provide the required slight fuzz texture and grit without heavy saturation.
blocks.gap: The Fuzz model is general; careful settings are needed to keep it from sounding too muddy or overly saturated, focusing on mid-range bite.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the Plexi/Marshall preamp tone and provide mid-forward crunch.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is a general boost; using it after Fuzz helps shape the core tone towards the desired British grit, compensating for the fuzz's inherent thickness.

blocks.purpose: Provide the core Marshall/Plexi-style amplification and punchy character.
Ground the tone with a classic British cabinet sound.
Wah is explicitly avoided by the musical verdict.
Keep the tone dry and focused on rhythm attack.
Add subtle note separation and definition without sounding wash-out.
blocks.gap: Used sparingly to enhance the 'punchy' feel, but kept very low to avoid excessive ambience.

blocks.purpose: Provide minimal space and prevent the tone from sounding too sterile, while maintaining dryness.
blocks.gap: The verdict calls for 'dry,' so reverb is kept at a minimum level to just add dimension.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism to better capture the punchy, dry Marshall/Plexi sound required for ZZ Top's rhythm tone.

proposals.reason: Enhance the punchy, dry Marshall character and mid-forward bite.
